*SERIOR Republic of the Philippines 9 DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT A. Francisco Gold Condominium II EDSA Cor. Mapagmahal St., Diliman Quezon City OFFICE OF THE UNDERSECRETARY FOR LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG OPINION no. 24 S. 2011 June 14, 2011 SANGGUNIANG BAYAN Macrohon, Leyte c/o Vice-Mayor ALAN JOSE K. AROY Gentlemen/Ladies: This has reference to your earlier letter requesting clarification and proper guidance as to the validity of an Ordinance entitled "An Ordinance Imposing TollFee on Any Non-Resident of Barangay Buscayan Who Shall Pass Thru the Two Barangay Roads, namely, Bernabe and Malbas Streets, in going to the Beach Resorts Down to the Seashore" passed by the Sangguniang Barangay of Barangay Buscayan, Macrohon, Leyte. Your letter was referred to the Central Office by Atty. Darwin N. Bibar, DILG-Region \JIII. Per the letter of Vice-Mayor Aroy, and its attachments, the Sangguniang Barangay of Barangay Buscayan enacted an Ordinance in 2009 imposing a toll fee on any non-resident of their barangay who shall pass thru the two (2) barangay roads namely, Bernabe and Malbas Streets, with the following rates: For Motor Vehicles: Motorcycles (any type) 3, Multicabl Jeepney, Cars, Trucks For Persons: 1. 2. Persons aged 10 years old and above Children below 10 years old Php 5.00 10.00 Php 1.00 - FREE In the Ordinance itself, it was provided that its purpose is to generate revenues for the rehabilitation, maintenance and improvement of the two (2) barangay roads that lead to the beach, namely, Bernabe St. and Malbas St. The subject Ordinance passed through the review of the Sangguniang Bayan that time. Meanwhile, the present set of Sangguniang Bayan holds the view that the subject Barangay Ordinance is substantial and legitimate based on DILG Memorandum Circular No. 2009-42, entitled "Imposition and collection of Local Taxes, Fees and Charges." However, you are now in a dilemma in view of DILG Memorandum Circular No, 2009-76 entitled "Reiterating Strict compliance to Pertinent Laws, Rules and DILG Circulars Prohibiting LGUs from Charging Fees on Passing through Vehicles Especially Those Carrying Agricultural Goods and Products and Exempting Vehicles from Truck ban Implementation". Hence, your request for clarification and proper guidance. May we note that the subject Barangay Ordinance was already approved as early as in 2009 or almost two (2) years now. In such cases, the Department shall refrain from taking action thereon in accordance with DILG Memorandum Order No. 2010-02 dated 17 September 2010 which supplements DILG Memorandum Order

No. 2010-01 dated 04 March 2010, since duly approved ordinances are presumptively valid acts and thus enjoy the presumption of regularity on the part of the public officer concerned, unless declared otherwise by our courts of justice upon proper judicial action. Be that as it may, for purposes of academic discussion coupled with the Department's objective to guide the parties on their proper action to take under the circumstances, we are of the view that the subject Ordinance enacted by Barangay Buscayan, Macrohon, Southern Leyte imposing a toll fee not only on the vehicles owned by the non-residents therein but also to the non-residents themselves who will go to beach resorts down to the seashore, is legally infirma We are of the view that the subject Ordinance is unfair or oppressive and unreasonable. By express language of Section 153 and 155 of the Local Government Code of 1991 (RA 7160), local government units, through their respective sanggunians, may prescribe the terms and conditions for the imposition of toll fees or charges for the use of any public road, pier or wharf funded and constructed by themi. A service fee imposed on vehicles using municipal roads leading to the wharf is thus valid2. Hence, it is thus apparent that a toll fee is a fee imposed on vehicles using public roads, not on passengers or persons. Along this line, DILG Memorandum Circular No. 2006-70 enjoins all local chief executives to "refrain from enforcing any existing ordinance authorizing the levy of fees and taxes on inter-province transport ofgoods, regulatory fees from passengers in local ports, and other additional taxes, fees or charges in any form upon transporting goods and passengers". For an ordinance to be valid, it must not only be within the corporate powers of the municipality or city to enact but must also be passed according to the procedure prescribed by law, and must be in consonance with certain well established and basic principles of a substantive nature. In the landmark case of Pryce Properties and Philippine Amusements and Gaming Magtajas vs. 3 the Supreme Court enumerated the following substantive Corporation requirements of a valid ordinance: (1) It must not contravene the constitution or any statute; (2) It must not be unfair or oppressive; (3) It must not be partial or discriminatory; (4) It must not prohibit but may regulate trade; (5) It must be general and consistent with public policy; and (6) It must not be unreasonable. Please be guided accordingly. Ls/17:28 Copy Furnished: ATTY. DARWIN N. BIBAR Chief, Finance and Administrative Division Officer-in-Charge DILG-Region VIII Kanhuraw Hills, Tacloban City Very t ly yours, AUSTERE A.
